title: Free entry, uncertain payoff
hook: A free entry and a paid entry use different stipulated win and loss rules.

knows: basic arithmetic and how to compare two stated rules
doesNotKnow: how to compare complete future outcomes rather than the free label

misconception: A zero entry price guarantees the highest overall expected return.
objective: Compare complete future outcomes rather than the free label.

claims.text: Original stipulated toy: Win and loss are net of every cost; points are fictional; repeated-trial average is not a single-trial guarantee. Paid-entry net outcomes already include its entry fee; no extra subtraction is due. Exact payoff inputs [{"label": "Free entry", "values": [20, 12, -3]}, {"label": "Paid entry", "values": [80, 5, -5]}]; second author arithmetic check A=0, B=3. Free entry averages {A}; paid entry {B}. Net outcomes include entry fees; different chances and consequences outweigh the free label. Plain-language prediction premise: Free entry has a 20% chance of +12 points and an 80% chance of -3. Over many entries under these rules, what is the mean net points per entry? The mean is probability-weighted: 0.2*12+0.8*(-3)=0 points per entry; this is not a guarantee for a single entry.
